BETHESDA, Md., Nov. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Gain Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: GANX) (“Gain”, or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biotechnology company leading the discovery and development of the next generation of allosteric small molecule therapies, today announced the presentation of two late-breaking posters at the 31st IAPRD World Congress on Parkinson’s Disease and Related Disorders as well as a poster at Neuroscience 2026.


**31** **st** **IAPRD World Congress on Parkinson’s Disease and Related Disorders**


Location: Milan, Italy


Date: November 11-14, 2026


Poster Title: “Open label extension of a Phase 1b clinical study to evaluate the effect of *rexaceract* (GT-02287) in Parkinson’s Disease”


Presentation Type: Guided Poster Tour


Poster Number: P9.8


Assigned Topic: Late Breakers


Date and Time: 3:30 – 4:30 p.m. CET, November 13


Poster Title: “Preclinical development of the novel GCase allosteric modulator GT-04686 in a GBA1 Parkinson’s disease model”


Presentation Type: Gallery Poster


Poster Number: P17.23


Assigned Topic: Parkinson’s Disease: Therapy (excluding surgical, physical)


**Neuroscience 2026**


Location: Washington, D.C.


Date: November 14-18, 2026


Poster Title: “Novel allosteric GCase modulator GT-04686 reduces neuropathology and improves motor and non-motor function in a preclinical model of GBA1 Parkinson’s disease”


Presentation Type: Poster


Presentation Number: PSTR222.06


Session Title: Parkinson’s Disease: Therapeutic Strategies in Preclinical Models


Session Date and Time: 8:00 a.m. – 12:00 p.m. EST, November 17


Presentation Time: 8:00 a.m. – 9:00 a.m. EST, November 17


**About the International Association of Parkinsonism and Related Disorders (IAPRD)’s 31** **st** **World Congress on Parkinson’s Disease and Related Disorders**
The IAPRD World Congress provides a collegial atmosphere to meet, interact and network with colleagues from around the world who are interested in the field of parkinsonism and related disorders. IAPRD 2026 will feature a program of clinical and scientific sessions revolving around the theme *Enhancing Patient Care Through Education, Technology, and Therapeutics.* A global faculty of distinguished experts will provide updates on the latest developments, current knowledge, and new tools enabling innovative research and treatment in parkinsonism and related disorders.


**About the SfN (Society for Neuroscience) ’s Neuroscience 2026 Annual Meeting**
The SfN annual meeting brings together scientists from around the world to discover new ideas, share their research, and experience the best the neuroscience field has to offer. Neuroscience 2026 will feature lectures, symposia, and events for scientists at all career stages.


**About Gain Therapeutics, Inc.**
Gain Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company leading the discovery and development of next generation allosteric therapies. Gain’s lead drug candidate, *rexaceract* is currently being evaluated for the treatment of PD with or without a GBA1 mutation in a Phase 1b clinical trial. *Rexaceract* has further potential in Gaucher’s disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, and Alzheimer’s disease. Gain has multiple undisclosed preclinical assets targeting lysosomal storage disorders, metabolic diseases, and solid tumors.


Gain’s unique approach enables the discovery of novel, allosteric small molecule modulators that can restore or disrupt protein function. Deploying its highly advanced Magellan™ platform, Gain is accelerating drug discovery and unlocking novel disease-modifying treatments for untreatable or difficult-to-treat disorders including neurodegenerative diseases, rare genetic disorders and oncology.
